summary.description: Create the core status emission system using contextvars for request-scoped status updates. This provides a simple, fire-and-forget API for emitting status updates from any async function without complex callback threading. The system mirrors the existing Langfuse tracing pattern with contextvars for async-safe operation across concurrent requests.
summary.business-value: Foundation for real-time status updates (Epic 11), enabling transparent visibility into Annie's processing phases, tool calls, and memory operations. This builds user trust and reduces wait anxiety.

criterion.title: emit_status() Function
criterion.requirements: - Callable from any async function without explicit parameters - Uses contextvars to find active status context - Fire-and-forget pattern with <10ms overhead - No-op if no context active (graceful degradation) - Accepts message string and optional icon parameter (default: "🔄")

criterion.title: with_status() Decorator
criterion.requirements: - Wraps async functions with status emission - Emits status on function entry - Supports string interpolation for dynamic messages (e.g., {tool_name}) - Preserves function signature and metadata using @wraps

criterion.title: StatusContext Manager
criterion.requirements: - Context manager that initializes status context for a request - Stores conversation_id for correlation - Provides callback mechanism for status delivery to SSE stream - Async-safe across concurrent requests using contextvars - Properly cleans up context on exit

criterion.title: Langfuse Integration
criterion.requirements: - Status emissions traced as spans in Langfuse - Links to parent request trace via existing tracing context - Non-blocking (follows existing fire-and-forget pattern)

pattern-reference.description: The status system follows the exact same pattern as Langfuse tracing: - Singleton ContextVar for request-scoped state (_status_context) - Fire-and-forget emission with graceful error handling - Async-safe isolation between concurrent requests - No manual context passing required
pattern-reference.key-concepts: - ContextVar isolation ensures each request has its own status emitter - Context manager (StatusContext) sets/resets token on enter/exit - emit_status() does contextvar lookup: _status_context.get(None) - Graceful degradation: no-op when no context active

point.description: StatusContext callback will write status frames to SSE stream. This story only creates the infrastructure - SSE integration happens in Story 11.2.
Reuse existing get_current_trace() from backend/api/observability/tracing.py to link status emissions as spans under the active request trace.

requirement.implementation: - No blocking I/O in emission path - Simple contextvar lookup (O(1)) - Callback execution is caller's responsibility - Try/except to prevent exceptions from propagating

pattern.name: ContextVar Singleton
pattern.example: # Request-scoped context variables (async-safe) _current_trace: ContextVar[Optional[Any]] = ContextVar('current_trace', default=None) # Stack of spans to handle nesting safely (immutable tuple) _span_stack: ContextVar[tuple] = ContextVar('span_stack', default=())

pattern.name: Fire-and-Forget Error Handling
pattern.example: try: trace = client.trace(name=name, user_id=user_id, session_id=session_id, metadata=metadata or {}) _current_trace.set(trace) logger.info(f"[LANGFUSE] Started trace: {name}", extra={...}) return trace except Exception as e: # Fire-and-forget: log warning but don't crash logger.warning(f"[LANGFUSE] Failed to start trace: {name}", extra={...}) return None
pattern.application: StatusEmitter.emit() should catch all exceptions and never fail. emit_status() should handle missing context gracefully.

pattern.name: Context Manager with Token
pattern.example:
class StatusContext: """Async context manager for status emission scope""" def __init__(self, conversation_id: str, callback: Callable[[str], None]): self.emitter = StatusEmitter(conversation_id, callback) self.token = None
async def __aenter__(self): self.token = _status_context.set(self.emitter) return self.emitter
async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb): _status_context.reset(self.token) return False
pattern.application: Use token pattern to ensure proper cleanup even on exceptions. Return False from __aexit__ to propagate exceptions.

pattern.name: Langfuse Client Singleton
pattern.example:
from api.observability.langfuse_client import get_langfuse_client
client = get_langfuse_client() if client: # Create span for status emission span = client.span(name="status_emission", metadata={"message": message})
pattern.application: Use get_langfuse_client() to check if tracing is enabled. Use get_current_trace() from tracing.py to link spans to active trace.

pattern.name: Decorator with @wraps
pattern.application: Use @wraps to preserve function metadata (name, docstring, signature). Decorator should work with async functions only.

- Implement emit_status(message: str, icon: str = "🔄") - Use _status_context.get() to retrieve emitter - Handle None case gracefully (no-op) - Format message as f"{icon} {message}" - Call emitter.emit() if context exists
- Create decorator factory accepting message and icon - Use @wraps(func) to preserve function metadata - Support async functions only - Call emit_status() on function entry - Return function result

- Create async context manager class - Accept conversation_id and status_callback parameters - Create StatusEmitter in __init__ - Set contextvar token in __aenter__ - Reset contextvar in __aexit__ - Handle exceptions gracefully (return False to propagate)

- Import get_current_trace from api.observability.tracing - In StatusEmitter.emit(), create span for each emission - Link span to current trace if available - Use fire-and-forget pattern (non-blocking) - Include message and icon in span metadata

implementation-notes.note: This story creates ONLY the infrastructure. No actual status emissions happen yet. Story 11.2 will integrate StatusContext into the SSE streaming route. Stories 11.4 and 11.5 will add status emissions to tool calls and memory operations.
The fire-and-forget pattern is critical: status emissions should NEVER block or crash the main request flow. All exceptions must be caught and logged.
ContextVar provides automatic async-safe isolation. No locks or manual context passing needed. Each concurrent request gets its own StatusEmitter via the context manager.
Langfuse integration is optional. If Langfuse is unavailable, status system still works (just without trace spans for status emissions).
